method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, inductive-definition and proof-tree reverse paraphrase, and exact formula, macro, token and identifier comparison; no independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Natural-deduction derivations: their inductive construction, finite-tree definition, discharged and undischarged assumptions, derivability notation, conjunction and conditional-introduction examples, and optional discharge.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Natural-deduction derivations are generated inductively from assumptions and inference rules: a derivation is either a lone assumption or one, two or three derivations followed by a correct inference.
samples.checks: The token-only heading remains source-identical and locale-driven; the base and inductive construction cases, arities and correctness requirement are explicit.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A derivation of sentence A from assumptions Gamma is a finite tree of sentences. Its top sentences belong to Gamma or are discharged; its bottom sentence is A; every other sentence is a premise of a correct inference whose conclusion is immediately below it. A is the conclusion and Gamma the undischarged assumptions. Existence yields Gamma proves A, while discharge of every assumption yields proves A.
samples.checks: All three defining conditions, premise/conclusion directions, the distinction between discharged and undischarged assumptions, and both provability formulas remain exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Each assumption is itself a derivation. Applying conjunction introduction to A and B gives A-and-B. Because the rule is schematic, C and D can replace A and B; swapping their roles instead gives D-and-C.
samples.checks: The three proof trees and every formula are unchanged; the prose preserves schematic replacement and the order-sensitive conclusions.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Conditional introduction derives a conditional and may discharge an assumption identical to its antecedent. The two trees respectively show D proves C implies C-and-D and C proves D implies C-and-D.
samples.checks: Both discharge labels, rule applications, antecedent relationship and the respective order of the two provability claims are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Discharging assumptions is optional. A discharge-capable rule may be applied even when the matching assumption is absent, so B may yield A-implies-B through conditional introduction without an A assumption to discharge.
samples.checks: The permission-versus-requirement contrast, absence condition and final proof tree remain explicit and exact.
